subject: Oceanography
title: Continental Drift
description: A fast breakdown of Continental Drift for builders.

hook.text: South America and Africa fit together like puzzle pieces—Alfred Wegener noticed this in 1912.

buildup.text: Wegener proposed that continents once formed a supercontinent called Pangaea—and slowly drifted apart.

discovery.text: Matching fossils, rock types, and glacial scratches on both sides of the Atlantic supported his idea.

twist.text: Scientists rejected Wegener for decades—he couldn't explain what force moved continents.

climax.text: It took until the 1960s and seafloor spreading to prove Wegener right.

punchline.text: The right idea, 50 years too early—the ocean floor proved it.

quiz.question: Who proposed the theory of continental drift?
